items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, we had a special guy, Bob, I don't know his last name.

ctx.x: Do you think that he -- I noticed that in listening to the recordings of Ellington's band, you all got a much better recording sound than a lot of other bands.

Yeah, we had a special guy, Bob, I don't know his last name. It wasn't like recording now. It had two notes, there wasn't no one guy off key. This guy -- Duke would stand off, when a guy over there was a little off, he would stop it and correct it. Not like now, all these bums that are playing "My mama and hey, baby, yagga dagga dagga." Because the worse you sound now, the more successful you are. But it wasn't like that. It had to be exact and perfect. Balance, tonation, everything. You get them guys, the…
